acceptance_criteria.criterion: When a project's detected folder name matches a declared repository's folder_names, the project list displays the repository's label instead of the raw folder name.
Projects with folder names not in any declared repository entry continue to display the raw folder name (no regression).
Multiple projects from different folder names that belong to the same declared repository display the same label.

summary: Implemented repository label resolution in the project list view.
Added `repoFolderMap` module-level variable (folder_name → {label, id}) populated on each load.
Modified `load()` to use `Promise.all` to fetch both projects and the repo registry in parallel; `listRepos()` failure is caught gracefully and falls back to an empty array (no crash).

Updated `buildTable` repo-column rendering: when a project's `repository_name` matches a registry folder_name, the label is displayed and linked to `#/strategy/:repoId`; unmatched folder names fall back to raw display.
Updated `renderList` test helper to inject per-URL mock data distinguishing `/api/repos` from `/api/projects`.
Added 5 new test cases covering all three acceptance criteria plus the fallback/degradation scenario.

comments.note: project-list.js: the `load()` function now fetches repos on every poll cycle (every 10 s). Since repository declarations change rarely, caching the repo registry with a longer TTL (e.g. only refetch when navigating away and back, or on explicit Refresh) would reduce unnecessary API calls. Not a correctness issue — worth noting for a future optimisation pass.

project-list.js: `repoFolderMap` is declared inside `renderProjectList` closure scope (not at module level). This is correct, but the variable is reset to `{}` at parse-time and then populated during `load()`. A concurrent poll cycle that starts before the first `load()` completes will briefly use an empty map, which is harmless but worth documenting.

tests/gui/project-list.test.ts: the `renderList` helper now uses a URL-discriminating fetch mock — a pattern not yet used by the other helpers in this file. If more two-endpoint views are added in future, extracting a shared `makeFetchMock(urlMap)` utility could reduce duplication.

Promise.all parallelises the two fetches; API.listRepos().catch(()=>[]) provides silent graceful degradation as required by AC-3.
Flat folder_name → {label, id} lookup map is the correct data structure for O(1) per-row resolution across multiple folder_names per repo.
buildTable repo cell correctly guards against null repo and missing registry entry; escapeHtml applied throughout.
renderList test helper URL-discriminating fetch mock is well-designed; consistent with existing test patterns in this file.

comments.note: load() fetches /api/repos on every 10s poll cycle. Since repo declarations change rarely, a longer-TTL cache (fetch only on navigation or explicit Refresh) would reduce API load. Low priority — correctness is not affected.

renderList() uses setTimeout(r, 20) to yield for microtask resolution. This timing-based approach is pragmatic and consistent with existing test patterns, but could become flaky on heavily loaded CI runners. A queueMicrotask-based drain or a test-specific promise flush would be more robust if new tests surface intermittent failures.
